messages.subject: Comparative Judgements
parts:
Is it possible to use the mirt package for modeling comparative judgment data? I have 150 texts where all are compared to each other by a large language model using the question 'Which text of the two is better?'. In total there are more than 11000 comparisons.

Thanks in advance,
Frank Bach

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Comparative Judgements
parts:
It's likely possible to do Thurstone IRT modeling with mirt, for example, though I have not tried to construct the syntax required for this (it's likely easier/faster to use the thurstoneIRT package by Paul Bürkner as fully Bayes code via Stan or lavaan code can be used). Otherwise, you can use unfolding models to do something similar for preference-type data (see Chen-Wei and I's article here discussing this topic, as well as the references therein: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0196292).

Phil
